newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bekaert sees 1996 profit near break-even.
newsitem.headline: Bekaert sees 1996 profit near break-even.

text.p: Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert said on Monday it expected 1996 current profit to be near break-even following provisions for a structural improvement programme.
"The required financial provision for this programme is estimated to reduce 1996 profit for the current operations close to break-even," the company said in a statement.

Bekaert said in September it did not expect a significant improvement in profitability for the second half of 1996 due to the slow improvement in steel wire and the weak demand in Europe for steel cord.

It said that since then, demand in Europe has weakened more than anticipated and increased competition from Eastern Europe further depressed shipped volumes and selling prices for steel cord and industrial steel wires.
The programme would be implemented "to cope with this situation and to strengthen its competitive position," the statement said.
Bekaert said in September that its first-half 1996 consolidated net profit fell to 1.3 billion francs from 1.8 billion in the year-earlier period.
It gave no first-half current profit figure.
Consolidated profit for 1996 however will benefit from the capital gain of 2.3 billion francs, announced in September, on the sale of shares in Japanese tyre-maker Bridgestone Metalpha Corp, it said.
Bekaert added that the expected benefit from its structural improvement programme would have a positive impact on 1997 earnings.
It said that the programme for its European steel wire and cord activities "focused on adapting its European production capacities to market needs and substantially reducing costs".
